physics_goals.value: Search for and characterize the quark-gluon plasma formed in heavy-ion collisions, and map the QCD phase diagram

summary.plain: PHENIX was one of the two large experiments at Brookhaven's RHIC collider, built from four merged detector proposals to study hot nuclear matter. It recorded its first collision in 2000 and stopped taking data in 2016.
summary.technical: Pioneering High Energy Nuclear Interaction eXperiment: a multi-arm heavy-ion collider spectrometer at RHIC IP8, formed in 1991 from the TALES/SPARC/OASIS/DIMUON proposal merger, combining central-arm and muon-arm detection to study quark-gluon plasma formation and the QCD phase diagram; recorded first collisions 2000-06-15 and completed data taking in 2016.

unique_capabilities.quote: August 1991: PHENIX is born from the merger of proposals named TALES, SPARC, OASIS, and DIMUON.
unique_capabilities.value: Formed from the 1991 merger of four separate detector proposals (TALES, SPARC, OASIS, DIMUON) into a single multi-arm spectrometer combining central-arm and forward muon-arm detection
